input: Learn to read a nutrition label properly

gold.taskTitle: Learn to read nutrition labels properly
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to understand how to correctly interpret the information on a nutrition facts label.

questions.title: What is your main reason for learning this skill?
questions.description: Understanding the motivation — weight loss, managing a health condition, eating cleaner, etc. — helps tailor the focus of the plan.

questions.title: Do you have a specific health condition to manage?
questions.description: Conditions like diabetes, hypertension, or high cholesterol require attention to specific nutrients such as sugar, sodium, or saturated fat.

questions.title: Which part of the label confuses you most right now?
questions.description: Identifying the sticking point — serving size, % Daily Value, ingredient order, etc. — lets us prioritize what to teach first.

questions.title: How familiar are you with basic nutrition concepts already?
questions.description: Knowing the user's baseline (complete beginner vs. some knowledge) determines how much foundational explanation is needed.

questions.title: Are there specific foods or categories you shop for most?
questions.description: Focusing examples on the user's actual shopping habits — snacks, frozen meals, cereals, etc. — makes the learning more practical and relevant.

questions.title: How do you prefer to learn new information?
questions.description: The user may prefer reading articles, watching videos, hands-on practice with real products, or a structured checklist.

questions.title: By when do you want to feel confident doing this?
questions.description: A target date or timeframe helps set a realistic pace and structure for the learning plan.
